name: multi-step-form
title: Multi-step form
purpose: A longer task split into steps shown one at a time: which step this is in words, the step's fields, Back and one primary action, and a review step before the final action.
whenToUse: For a task with more fields than fit one view comfortably, where later steps depend on earlier answers, such as choosing a repository before writing the task.
When the final action is costly or hard to undo, so the reader should see everything they chose before it runs.
For three to five steps. Each step is its own address, so the browser's back button and a reload both work.
whenNotToUse: For a form that fits one view. Use fields and a button group on one page, and put rarely changed fields in one advanced disclosure.
For one question or one field. Use a dialog.
For settings the reader changes one at a time. Use the settings page.
For sections the reader may fill in any order. Use one page with headings.
accessibility: In an app the element with gw-multi-step-form is the main element. The h1 names the whole task and is the same on every step. Each step is one form, with an h2 that names the step.

gw-multi-step-form__step is a p directly above the h2 that reads Step 2 of 4, in words. When a step loads, move focus to the h2, which takes tabindex="-1", so a screen reader reads the step's name, and put the step in the document title.
To show the named steps above the form, with the completed and current ones marked, use the stepper component. Keep the step line in words as well.

Every step ends with a button group. The secondary action comes first: Back, a link to the previous step that keeps what was typed, or Cancel on the first step. The primary action comes last: Continue on every step but the last.

The last step is the review. It shows every answer in a key-value list, in the order the steps asked for them, then one sentence on what the final action does. Its primary button is a specific verb and what it acts on, such as Start task, never Submit or Finish.

Validate a step when it is sent. Keep the reader on the step, add an alert with role="alert" above the fields whose title counts the fields to fix and whose body names them, mark each field with aria-invalid="true" and its own error message, and move focus to the first invalid field.
A field's error says how to fix the value. Remove the error and aria-invalid when the value is fixed, and remove the alert when none is left.
While a step is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the primary button and change its label to say what is happening, such as Starting task.
Nothing the reader must fill in sits inside a closed disclosure. A step may hold one advanced disclosure for optional fields that have defaults.
Tab moves through the fields in order, then Back, then the primary action. Enter in a text input sends the step. The pattern needs no script of its own.
